items.label: Turning Points 02
items.summary: BBC Radio Cambridgeshire, 2019, live. The quiet son who never spoke up, on air across the county. So what changed?

items.label: Turning Points 03
items.summary: Every test came back normal. Every doctor said I was fine. Every part of me said I wasn't.

items.label: Turning Points 04
items.summary: New Zealand, 2005. My cousin's wedding, and I'd been asked to be the MC. That's how I met Liril.

items.label: Turning Points 05
items.summary: Not for university. Not for my first job. Not once. Comfort doesn't feel like a cage. It feels like love.

items.label: Science and Spirit 02
items.summary: 6/6 is the line on the chart we all aim for. For a long time, I thought it meant a job well done. It doesn't.

items.label: Turning Points 06
items.summary: 2001. A borrowed house in St Neots, and my first time living away from my parents. It was frightening.

items.label: Turning Points 07
items.summary: Ten till five. Free parking. Fifteen minutes from home. I could have stayed there for the rest of my career.

items.label: Science and Spirit 03
items.summary: Every time you blink, a film thinner than a hair keeps your eye seeing. Tears are not a weakness.

items.label: Turning Points 08
items.summary: It began with a moment of kindness. And a mistake.

items.label: Turning Points 09
items.summary: 2017 was one of the hardest years I have known. So I took the small opportunities in front of me.

items.label: Turning Points 10
items.summary: There's one name missing from every trophy we've ever lifted. Everyone's.

items.label: Science and Spirit 04
items.summary: Pass white light through a prism and it opens into a rainbow. The colours were there all along.

items.label: Turning Points 11
items.summary: In 2020, at 42, I began training as an Independent Prescriber. Twenty years after qualifying, I sat exams again.

items.label: Turning Points 12
items.summary: I walked in expecting to share what I knew. Week after week, I walked out having learned more than I taught.

items.label: Turning Points 13
items.summary: Some days, work is the calmest place in my life.

items.label: The Inner Journey 01
items.summary: What if spiritual growth isn't about becoming someone new, but rediscovering who we were before the world shaped us?

items.label: Turning Points 14
items.summary: When people meet me, they see the suit, the smile, the practice.

items.label: The Inner Journey 02
items.summary: We have become experts at thinking. But have we forgotten how to be still?

items.label: Turning Points 15
items.summary: When my sons were small, they followed me everywhere.

items.label: The Inner Journey 03
items.summary: There's always another achievement waiting to make us happy. So why does satisfaction stay just out of reach?

items.label: Turning Points 16
items.summary: My parents live across the road from us now.

items.label: The Inner Journey 04
items.summary: It's possible to know a great deal about life and still struggle to guide your own.

items.label: Turning Points 17
items.summary: My father met his own father properly only as a young man. Within a year, he had died.

items.label: The Inner Journey 05
items.summary: Our closest relationships often teach us our greatest lessons about love.

items.label: Turning Points 18
items.summary: My grandmother was married at twelve or thirteen.

items.label: The Inner Journey 06
items.summary: We remember the words that hurt us. How often do we remember the words we've used to hurt others?

items.label: Turning Points 19
items.summary: From the outside, my early twenties looked fine. I'd qualified as an optometrist. I had a profession, a family, a future.

items.label: The Inner Journey 07
items.summary: How much of our present are we giving away to something that happened in the past?

items.label: Science and Spirit 05
items.summary: Walk from a bright room into darkness, and at first you see nothing. Then, slowly, shapes appear. The edge of a door. A chair. A window.

items.label: The Inner Journey 08
items.summary: What if peace begins when we stop demanding an answer to every question?

items.label: Science and Spirit 06
items.summary: Hold your gaze on a single word on this page.

items.label: The Inner Journey 09
items.summary: Can we truly grow spiritually if it makes us less compassionate towards others?

items.label: The Inner Journey 10
items.summary: Spiritual growth isn't a straight line. It's a living process.
